title: Tax on Gifted and Inherited Real Estate 2026: Exemptions and 10% Rate
desc: Gifted or inherited real estate in 2026: PIT and registration fee exemptions for relatives, 10% above VND 20 million for others, and how value is set.
summary: How personal income tax and registration fees are calculated when receiving gifted or inherited real estate under the Personal Income Tax Law 2025 and Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
body: A parent gives a house to a child, a grandparent leaves land to a grandchild, or an uncle gives a nephew a plot of land: each case carries different tax obligations. From 1 July 2026, the rules follow Personal Income Tax Law No. 109/2025/QH15 and Decree 253/2026/ND-CP.
1. Is tax payable on inherited or gifted real estate?

Income from receiving inherited or gifted real estate is taxable personal income tax (PIT) income (Clause 9, Article 3 of the PIT Law). Real estate includes land use rights, land with attached assets, houses (including homes to be built in the future), construction works, land lease rights, and so on (Clause 3, Article 15 of Decree 253/2026/ND-CP). The recipient is the taxpayer.
Tax is exempt on gifts and inheritance of real estate between (Clause 1, Article 4; Article 18 of Decree 253/2026/ND-CP):
Husband and wife; biological parents and biological children; adoptive parents and adopted children.
Parents-in-law and daughter-in-law (even if the husband has died); parents-in-law and son-in-law (even if the wife has died).
Paternal grandparents and paternal grandchildren; maternal grandparents and maternal grandchildren; siblings.
Real estate divided on a couple's divorce, by agreement or court judgment, is also exempt. Note: uncles, aunts and nephews or nieces, and cousins are not on the exemption list.

Tax = (value of the real estate received − VND 20 million) × 10%, calculated for each receipt (Article 18 of the PIT Law; Clauses 1 and 2, Article 61 of Decree 253/2026/ND-CP). Non-resident individuals are also taxed at 10% on the amount above VND 20 million (Article 26).
The value of the real estate is determined at the time of completing the registration of the use right or ownership (Point c, Clause 4, Article 61):
The land: according to the provincial land price list and land price adjustment coefficient (if any).

The house or building: according to the price used for house registration fees set by the provincial People's Committee; if the province has not set one, according to the Ministry of Construction's rules and the actual remaining value.

Example: a nephew receives a gift of a house and land from his uncle (his father's brother), with the land valued at VND 1 billion by the price list and the house at VND 200 million by the registration fee price. PIT = (VND 1,200 million − VND 20 million) × 10% = VND 118 million.
4. Registration fee when registering the transfer

On registration, the recipient also pays a registration fee of 0.5% (Clause 1, Article 8 of Consolidated Document 33/VBHN-BTC), except when receiving inheritance or gifts between relatives as in section 2 (Clause 10, Article 10). In the example above, if the price for the registration fee is also VND 1,200 million, the fee is VND 1,200 million × 0.5% = VND 6 million. See Registration fee on real estate 2026.
Tax is calculated for each occurrence (Point b, Clause 1, Article 66).
Income from inheritance and gifts is not withheld at source; the recipient declares and pays tax under tax administration law (Clauses 4 and 5, Article 67).

Even where exempt, an exemption dossier must still be filed under tax administration law (Clause 3, Article 18); it is advisable to prepare birth certificates, marriage certificates, and so on to prove the relationship.
If the transaction is a sale rather than a gift, the obligation is a 2% tax on the transfer price; see Personal income tax when selling real estate 2026.

This article is a summary for reference only and does not replace legal documents. Dossiers and tax filing deadlines follow tax administration law (not yet in our library). The PIT Law 109/2025/QH15 is shown as partially no longer in force on the National Legal Portal; the exact tax is notified by the tax authority.
